headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if marker consumes langchain4j-generated content as instructions; otherwise most other pairwise risks are low or none.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, langchain4j can mediate LLM workflows and marker is a runnable document processor; if outputs are manually bridged or placed in a shared workspace, marker could parse attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the two agents are connected by copy-paste, shared files, or another bridge that passes raw text from langchain4j into marker
IF marker treats document text or extracted text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff of raw text between agents
Add a delimiter/template that strips instructions from document content
Review one sample handoff for prompt-like text before production
Use a human approval step for any instruction-bearing payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none, and marker also cannot read or write the filesystem. Langchain4j has no documented filesystem or data-class exposure here, so there is no plausible pairwise leakage path in the provided profiles. The evidence does not support a shared sensitive-data flow.
conditions: IF either profile is later granted filesystem access to sensitive data
IF either agent is reconfigured to send contents to a third-party backend
mitigations: Keep both agents on local-only inference
Do not mount sensitive directories into either agent
Verify egress remains disabled in deployment
Add a quick audit of runtime permissions before launch

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and langchain4j has no documented write or git capabilities in the profile. With no overlapping mutable write surface, the pair cannot conflict over shared state as described by the rubric.
conditions: IF marker is later granted write access to a shared directory
IF langchain4j is deployed with a writable shared workspace or git automation
mitigations: Keep marker read-only
Avoid shared writable directories
Separate any git automation from both agents
Recheck permissions after deployment changes

D_cascading_error.rationale: A plausible cascade exists if langchain4j-generated text is fed into marker and then rendered or acted on without verification. Langchain4j can produce model outputs, while marker is a document-processing agent that may consume those outputs as authoritative content. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF marker consumes langchain4j output as authoritative input without a verification step
IF downstream systems act on marker's extracted text or summaries
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require source citations for any extracted claims
Compare a sample output against the original document
Route high-impact actions to a human reviewer

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so no compliance mismatch can be established from the profiles. Because the rubric requires a concrete mismatch, the absence of such fields makes this pathway unproven rather than risky.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII
IF residency or retention policies are added and differ between the two agents
mitigations: Document data-class handling for both agents
Record residency and retention settings before deployment
Block regulated data until policies are reviewed
Reassess compliance after any policy change
